routing_warnings.description: This message directs work to continue through higher grades rather than changing curriculum-alignment rules.
This message concerns the quality of the reusable content-generation prompt.
The all-grades clause establishes the breadth of Toy Factory grade coverage rather than modifying curriculum-alignment criteria.
The freelancer claims Grade 3 topics and their levels were added, but does not claim that their curriculum alignment was verified.
Continuing from Grade 2 to higher grades concerns grade coverage rather than the rules for progression within a topic.
Coverage of all grades for the Toy Factory mini game is owned by the separate grade-coverage Requirement.
Adding Grade 3 topics and levels is a grade-coverage implementation claim and does not specifically establish curriculum-based segmentation or progression.
This message establishes how a question applying to several levels must be repeated in the spreadsheet, rather than changing the one-question-specification-per-level rule.
Together with message 68, this client acceptance establishes that every level needs a different object, not that its representation type must be classified.
The freelancer claims that objects were included in the questions but does not state that representation types were classified.
The update explicitly mentions objects but does not identify the representation-type classification behavior.
This message specifies mathematical problem types for the sorting activity rather than requirements for the reusable ChatGPT prompt.
This implementation claim concerns revised level objectives and does not claim completion of the ChatGPT prompt.
This message reports generation of Grade 3 and Grade 4 topic content rather than implementation of the reusable prompt.
Dividing the number range into three similar levels concerns level progression rather than accepted sorting-problem content.
The 0-to-20 level range belongs to the curriculum-based level-progression Requirement.
The 20-to-50 level range belongs to the curriculum-based level-progression Requirement.
The 50-to-100 level range belongs to the curriculum-based level-progression Requirement.
Coverage of all grades is owned by the independently defined all-grade Toy Factory coverage Requirement.
The separate claim that objects were updated may also support the visual-object Requirement.
